## How to append

1. Relevance-check the delta (DAGKnight / Argent / SilverScript / KCC focus).
2. Edit `master.json` / README only when material; always add a newest-first row here. In the README, rewrite the short **Now** cell to the current state (a few sentences, key hashes and links); do not append dated lines to it. Longer text moved out of a cell goes verbatim under a dated heading at the end of this file. [`RECEIPTS.md`](RECEIPTS.md) is frozen.
3. Commit + push `STP-KAS/kaspa-master-file`.
4. If masterfile changed, short pointer on `kaspa-dapps` + `project-delusional` when needed.
5. Tell stp in chat: commit SHA, what changed, pins hold or not.

Local checkout (when present): `/workspace/artifacts/stp-kas/kaspa-master-file/`

Not merged. Not a release.

The comment says a signed compare treats `0x80` as negative zero and `0xff` as -127, so `>= 0` still accepts `0x80`. `transfer_validates_output_schemes_across_full_byte_domain` loops every byte `0..=255` for both output fields. [`ebcba45d`](https://github.com/argent-lang/kcc20-reference/commit/ebcba45d99987060e95c440b3ddd7dd50e578d06) keeps the amount threshold on the borrow path. A negative threshold, and the negative-zero guard with byte 7 set to `0x80`, clamps to zero. The token increase must be strictly positive. A normal transfer still accepts a negative threshold guard. The threshold is the first eight guard bytes. [`a0d6a8c3`](https://github.com/argent-lang/kcc20-reference/commit/a0d6a8c353981629e3ebedecf52ffdffd7b6e92f) (7 Oct 08:38Z) makes `KCC20PublicMint` the only app and starts tracking `fixtures/public-mint/`. [`ba8f06e6`](https://github.com/argent-lang/kcc20-reference/commit/ba8f06e657eca6e2dedf58ee553ec7e6125a7e42) adds permissionless `PublicMint.split`. The call carries no owner signature. `take` is positive and `<= remaining / 2`. The retained output keeps the owner and the KAS value. The added output receives `take`, a caller-chosen owner, and caller-funded KAS. The two remainings sum to the previous remaining. The half cap is per call. `mint` stays permissionless on each deposit. The owner key reclaims the KAS: `reclaim` requires `remaining == 0` and `checkSig`, and `reclaim_into` lets the survivor lead with no signature while the retiring owner signs `reclaim_delegator`. `TokenSeed.create` requires amount zero. It builds a receiving UTXO. The supply comes from `mint`. Seed `split` is permissionless and has no half cap. Seed `reclaim` consumes a retiring seed and recreates the leader, so a lone seed has no reclaim. The lifecycle test `minter_split_mint_and_reclaim_return_unused_allowance` builds the split with no signature, rejects `take` 13 from remaining 25, and accepts `take` 7. One buggy instance is not a verdict on the script engine, and it is not “KCC-20 shipped.” Same morning he separated KRC-20 (off-chain interpretation) from covenants. Catalog, not a status change. The file is **Last Call** on main [`3fbec524`](https://github.com/kaspanet/kccs/commit/3fbec524abfbc20e87652eb938db218f8c17db17) since [#31](https://github.com/kaspanet/kccs/pull/31) (7 Oct 20:38Z), not Final. **11 Oct, KRC-20 to KCC-20 migration (Sutton's statement):** replying to GabrielNico21 ([2109049463302156773](https://x.com/GabrielNico21/status/2109049463302156773), 10 Oct 22:32:30Z), who asked whether a token can still migrate to KCC20 if its KRC-20 minting is unfinished, Sutton ([2109305350008475670](https://x.com/michaelsuttonil/status/2109305350008475670), 11 Oct 15:29:19Z / 17:29:19 CEST) wrote: "yes it can migrate with the same rules. it will need a custom migration with the target KCC-20 contracts supporting the same public minting policy over the remaining supply. (my answer is not specific to some migration proposed by specific entities which i know nothing about; it’s about the conceptual question)" **11 Oct, KCC-20 vs Solana (Sutton's statement):** HuseyinSivridag asked ([2109311950651834538](https://x.com/HuseyinSivridag/status/2109311950651834538), 15:55:32Z / 17:55:32 CEST): "Will the Kcc20 smart contract language possess the full smart contract capabilities of Solana?" Sutton replied ([2109315001034875348](https://x.com/michaelsuttonil/status/2109315001034875348), 16:07:40Z / 18:07:40 CEST), full text: "not easily, no. a solana program has more capabilities and can be longer and more expressive. sophisticated designs can create a multi-contract argent app that executes complex behavior across partitioned state and over multiple transactions (that’s why i called these “mini programs”), like i did with chess, but then composition with other covenants/apps needs to be carefully designed, as does contention over shared variables/state.<br>in short, i cannot promise you yet that things will run smoothly and compose cleanly. we are not a solana vm by design, and hence i expect the created apps/systems to be shaped differently to match the inherent constraints. so i can’t promise how exactly this will evolve, but my strong hypothesis is that it enables significantly complicated systems.<br>(the answer above is all within pure covenants and does not talk about based zk apps, which are as fully expressive as a solana program but currently have limited L1 composability that depends on zk proof submission)" His follow-up ([2109316491417878839](https://x.com/michaelsuttonil/status/2109316491417878839), 16:13:35Z / 18:13:35 CEST) is only a link to a [Grok share](https://x.com/i/grok/share/c2hhcmQtMw_fffeb959-8edf-4095-a5e0-2b7aa514d983); its content was not read here, so it is not described. The earlier post where he called them "mini programs" is not in this file. Desk reading, hedged, not his words: his answer is "not easily, no"; he says a Solana program has more capabilities and can be longer and more expressive, and that sophisticated designs can split an Argent app across several contracts, partitioned state and multiple transactions; he does not promise clean composition, but states a "strong hypothesis" that it enables significantly complicated systems; the answer covers pure covenants only, and he calls based ZK apps as fully expressive as a Solana program but with limited L1 composability today. Chess is his example, not desk-checked. Prior cell: [SNAPSHOT-HISTORY](SNAPSHOT-HISTORY.md#now-row-kcc-20-wording-as-of-11-oct-2026-before-the-sutton-solana-rewrite).

### Now row "KCC-20 wording" (as of 11 Oct 2026, before the 12 Oct rewrite)

Michael Sutton, [20 Sep](https://x.com/michaelsuttonil/status/2101641365419417797): a properly written KCC-20 covenant gets L1 enforcement of those rules; KCC-20 itself is a spec. One buggy instance is not a verdict on the script engine, and it is not “KCC-20 shipped.” Same morning he separated KRC-20 (off-chain interpretation) from covenants. Catalog, not a status change. The file is **Last Call** on main [`3fbec524`](https://github.com/kaspanet/kccs/commit/3fbec524abfbc20e87652eb938db218f8c17db17) since [#31](https://github.com/kaspanet/kccs/pull/31) (7 Oct 20:38Z), not Final. **11 Oct, KRC-20 to KCC-20 migration (Sutton's statement):** replying to GabrielNico21 ([2109049463302156773](https://x.com/GabrielNico21/status/2109049463302156773), 10 Oct 22:32:30Z), who asked whether a token can still migrate to KCC20 if its KRC-20 minting is unfinished, Sutton ([2109305350008475670](https://x.com/michaelsuttonil/status/2109305350008475670), 11 Oct 15:29:19Z / 17:29:19 CEST) wrote: "yes it can migrate with the same rules. it will need a custom migration with the target KCC-20 contracts supporting the same public minting policy over the remaining supply. (my answer is not specific to some migration proposed by specific entities which i know nothing about; it’s about the conceptual question)" **11 Oct, KCC-20 vs Solana (Sutton's statement):** HuseyinSivridag asked ([2109311950651834538](https://x.com/HuseyinSivridag/status/2109311950651834538), 15:55:32Z / 17:55:32 CEST): "Will the Kcc20 smart contract language possess the full smart contract capabilities of Solana?" Sutton replied ([2109315001034875348](https://x.com/michaelsuttonil/status/2109315001034875348), 16:07:40Z / 18:07:40 CEST), full text: "not easily, no. a solana program has more capabilities and can be longer and more expressive. sophisticated designs can create a multi-contract argent app that executes complex behavior across partitioned state and over multiple transactions (that’s why i called these “mini programs”), like i did with chess, but then composition with other covenants/apps needs to be carefully designed, as does contention over shared variables/state.<br>in short, i cannot promise you yet that things will run smoothly and compose cleanly. we are not a solana vm by design, and hence i expect the created apps/systems to be shaped differently to match the inherent constraints. so i can’t promise how exactly this will evolve, but my strong hypothesis is that it enables significantly complicated systems.<br>(the answer above is all within pure covenants and does not talk about based zk apps, which are as fully expressive as a solana program but currently have limited L1 composability that depends on zk proof submission)" His follow-up ([2109316491417878839](https://x.com/michaelsuttonil/status/2109316491417878839), 16:13:35Z / 18:13:35 CEST) is only a link to a [Grok share](https://x.com/i/grok/share/c2hhcmQtMw_fffeb959-8edf-4095-a5e0-2b7aa514d983); its content was not read here, so it is not described. The earlier post where he called them "mini programs" is not in this file. Desk reading, hedged, not his words: his answer is "not easily, no"; he says a Solana program has more capabilities and can be longer and more expressive, and that sophisticated designs can split an Argent app across several contracts, partitioned state and multiple transactions; he does not promise clean composition, but states a "strong hypothesis" that it enables significantly complicated systems; the answer covers pure covenants only, and he calls based ZK apps as fully expressive as a Solana program but with limited L1 composability today. Chess is his example, not desk-checked. Prior cell: [SNAPSHOT-HISTORY](SNAPSHOT-HISTORY.md#now-row-kcc-20-wording-as-of-11-oct-2026-before-the-sutton-solana-rewrite). **Cross-links (11 Oct):** the migration reply goes with the KRC-20 to KCC row (Sutton's 19 Aug snapshot preference, manyfest's proposal). His "contention over shared variables/state" is the open question of Kas-Smiths topic [160](https://kas-smiths.org/t/high-bps-covenant-state-pressure-utxo-contention-storage-mass-and-settlement-frequency-seeking-corrections/160) (weirdtualguy, 9 Oct 20:42Z: covenant UTXO contention, storage mass at 10 BPS, MEV; 1 post, no replies at the 11 Oct 17:13Z read); see Kas-Smiths. Topic 160 does not discuss migration, so the migration reply is not linked to it. Per the PR text (atharaldsen): blocks synced by IBD go from sync_missing_block_bodies straight to consensus and never through FlowContext::on_new_block; only high priority (RPC-submitted) txs are revalidated periodically, so a relayed tx accepted that way stays in the mempool with its inputs spent until the 24h expiry; a mining node recovers on its next block template, a node that never builds templates does not. The fix revalidates the whole mempool as the last step of IbdFlow::ibd, without rebroadcasting. State span is `0+0`. Template hash is `15c6d0e9953deeec78183715e20ff0ce66306246f41cf7149cf4d8ec19a1add8`. The compiler prints no warning. Offline desk test 10 Oct 10:14–10:16 CEST at 01b532e8 https://github.com/kaspanet/rusty-kaspa/commit/01b532e8b553523216471682649693af92f0fd16 (commit read from the scratch checkout after the run, not in the logs; rustc 1.98.1 48a229cea per the run log; a scratch kaspa-txscript test that is not upstream; no node, no broadcast) on the gist https://gist.github.com/michaelsutton/04edba7e112756088c515b2949db267b/c2ae033802e7f1c6f6453cb665a32a4b30788d19 script: a SIG_HASH_ALL spend passed engine execution, a wrong pubkey failed with VerifyError (OP_EQUALVERIFY) and a wrong-key signature with EvalFalse (OP_CHECKSIG), and ScriptClass::from_script returned NonStandard; a desk result, not a consensus or standardness change. Gist, not a KIP.

In `consensus/src/model/stores/utxo_set.rs`, a new `UtxoImportWriter` buffers writes in one RocksDB `WriteBatch` and writes it to the DB when it reaches 1000 entries or 1 MiB (`1 << 20` bytes), and once more at the end of each call. It is used only by two new IBD methods: `write_imported_chunk` (pruning-point import, from `consensus/mod.rs`) and `copy_imported_from_iterator` (copy into virtual, from `virtual_processor/processor.rs`). Ordinary UTXO writes keep their writer. `utxo_set/import_tests.rs` checks that batched imports give the same rows as direct writes, including last-write-wins across a batch boundary, and that the copy path updates the cache. It also checks that the writer flushes at the entry and byte bounds and keeps the tail until the final flush. A third disk benchmark test is `#[ignore]`. Draft, not merged; the ~16% is the author's figure.

### Prior cell: KRC-20 incident (to 15 Oct 2026)

**Not an L1 exploit.** 20 Sep: the ZealousSwap post-mortem, as relayed by Recon [2101642546803863779](https://x.com/ReconProtocol/status/2101642546803863779), traces it to a signature bypass in the off-chain Kasplex KRC-20 indexer, not Kaspa L1. KRC-20 token state is interpreted by indexers, not by L1 consensus. Third-party report. The desk did not read the post-mortem itself. Kasplex's indexer fix release (go-krc20d) and later commits are third-party product status: kaspa-builders [entries/krc20-incident.md](https://github.com/STP-KAS/kaspa-builders/blob/main/entries/krc20-incident.md) (not merged there yet).

### Prior cell: Launch proof and binding (to 16 Oct 2026)

Sutton [2081846048280965268](https://x.com/michaelsuttonil/status/2081846048280965268) (27 Jul): every deployed L1 covenant should come with a launch proof derived from its covenant-id preimage, covering the full contracts and initial state, and with inspectable source. [2082066262520463670](https://x.com/michaelsuttonil/status/2082066262520463670) (28 Jul): the UTXO carries the covenant id (its preimage proves the launch) and the spk (p2sh commits to the contract/actor and its state). [2087453635206643755](https://x.com/michaelsuttonil/status/2087453635206643755) (12 Aug): a DEX binds each whitelisted asset by the pair (template hash, covenant id). The template is passed at runtime as an untrusted sig arg and checked against the hash. Example: [argent-playground `dex.ag` L32 at `0a2e80d1`](https://github.com/argent-lang/argent-playground/blob/0a2e80d13ac8394a62057f21db954be17bcbf994/ag/dex/dex.ag#L32). [2098077295214809214](https://x.com/michaelsuttonil/status/2098077295214809214) (10 Sep) links the formal analysis [`leader-delegate-input-groups.md`](https://github.com/argent-lang/argent/blob/master/docs/security-invariants/leader-delegate-input-groups.md) on argent master (#60, merged 10 Sep). The covenant-state provenance doc behind the silverscript#234 close is only on branch [`covenant-state-provenance`](https://github.com/argent-lang/argent/blob/covenant-state-provenance/docs/security-invariants/covenant-state-provenance.md) (`35bec64a`, 3 Sep), not on master ([Sutton](https://x.com/michaelsuttonil/status/2095472062701699101)). Sutton [2106033659698450492](https://x.com/michaelsuttonil/status/2106033659698450492) (2 Oct 14:48Z) points at [argent#66](https://github.com/argent-lang/argent/pull/66) (genesis-proof tooling, then open at head `9592dd99`) and expects every stateful covenant to publish that link. Sutton merged #66 on 4 Oct 12:04Z (14:04 CEST) as [`03d67021`](https://github.com/argent-lang/argent/commit/03d670217b7139ee452e1c50d109f600ed85d94d) (PR head `aab8fe1e`, two commits past `9592dd99`). No tag. **5 Oct, two covenant categories (Sutton):** [2107218445993738378](https://x.com/michaelsuttonil/status/2107218445993738378) (21:16Z): some covenants are about the Kaspa they protect (vaults, timelocks, escrow), others about the state they carry, which forms another mini social consensus (name services, native KCC-20 tokens). A timelock has no forgery problem, because anyone may clone the script over their own KAS; when the state itself matters, imitation does, and that is why Toccata introduced covenant ids and covenant lineage ([2107246681162948905](https://x.com/michaelsuttonil/status/2107246681162948905), 23:08Z). The genesis preimage shows the birth was right, but it matters only because the covenant id gives provable lineage ([2107241339066671607](https://x.com/michaelsuttonil/status/2107241339066671607)). A privacy pool and a based app are both kinds at once: state (notes and nullifiers; external state) plus a pool of KAS (for a based app, the canonical bridge) ([2107231201165549636](https://x.com/michaelsuttonil/status/2107231201165549636)). Native state-carrying covenants can already support assets, DEXs and lending ([2107239797513236579](https://x.com/michaelsuttonil/status/2107239797513236579)). In a separate, earlier reply (18:40Z, another conversation), P2SH also compresses: the launch of a complex app with several continuation contracts folds under 32 initial bytes ([2107179238440976510](https://x.com/michaelsuttonil/status/2107179238440976510)). On randomness ([2107237888304013388](https://x.com/michaelsuttonil/status/2107237888304013388), 22:33Z): PoW block hashes are a good source only if the mechanism cannot choose which hashes it uses; reading them from the script engine is tricky but not impossible; based apps have an easier path through the KIP-21 sequencing commitment, again without giving the mechanism or the zk prover selection power. X replies, his reading; not a KIP. In the same thread Manyfest ([2107373867396182019](https://x.com/manyfest_/status/2107373867396182019), 6 Oct 07:34Z): for the first kind the node itself checks that no KAS is created in the transition; for the second, the genesis tx creates new "matter" the node knows nothing about, so the covenant logic must enforce its conservation, and other covenants can compose on it. Asked how a user knows a contract hides no backdoor such as a `terminate()` paying the developer, Sutton answered "no doubt. hence" and quoted his 2 Oct genesis-proof post 2106033659698450492 ([2107536837522678263](https://x.com/michaelsuttonil/status/2107536837522678263), 6 Oct 18:21Z). Catalog. **Reasoning kept from a moved project:** covenant id derivation, desk recompute 3 Oct (no node) on a third-party Testnet-10 registry genesis: blake2b-256 keyed `CovenantID` over the authorizing outpoint, then each authorized output's index, value and script public key (not its covenant binding), per rusty-kaspa v2.1.0 [covenant_id.rs](https://github.com/kaspanet/rusty-kaspa/blob/01b532e8b553523216471682649693af92f0fd16/consensus/core/src/hashing/covenant_id.rs) ([hashers.rs L32](https://github.com/kaspanet/rusty-kaspa/blob/01b532e8b553523216471682649693af92f0fd16/crypto/hashes/src/hashers.rs#L32)); any change to those outputs gives a different id, and the recomputed id matched the published one. Details: see [STP-KAS/kaspa-builders](https://github.com/STP-KAS/kaspa-builders) (entry name-services). **Desk note 6 Oct, covenant lineage in rusty-kaspa v2.1.0 `01b532e8` (desk reading, not a KIP):** an output may carry covenant id X only if its authorizing input's UTXO already carries X (continuation, [covenants.rs L124-136](https://github.com/kaspanet/rusty-kaspa/blob/01b532e8b553523216471682649693af92f0fd16/crypto/txscript/src/covenants.rs#L124-L136)) or X equals the id recomputed from that input's outpoint and the group's authorized outputs (genesis, [L137-160](https://github.com/kaspanet/rusty-kaspa/blob/01b532e8b553523216471682649693af92f0fd16/crypto/txscript/src/covenants.rs#L137-L160); [covenant_id.rs L16-30](https://github.com/kaspanet/rusty-kaspa/blob/01b532e8b553523216471682649693af92f0fd16/consensus/core/src/hashing/covenant_id.rs#L16-L30)); otherwise the tx fails with `WrongGenesisCovenantId`. This runs for every tx in UTXO context ([tx_validation_in_utxo_context.rs L58](https://github.com/kaspanet/rusty-kaspa/blob/01b532e8b553523216471682649693af92f0fd16/consensus/src/processes/transaction_validator/tx_validation_in_utxo_context.rs#L58)). An outpoint is spent once, so every UTXO carrying X descends through authorizing-input links from one genesis; that is the lineage. `OpCovInputCount` (0xd0) pushes the number of tx inputs whose UTXO carries the given id ([opcodes/mod.rs L1333-1341](https://github.com/kaspanet/rusty-kaspa/blob/01b532e8b553523216471682649693af92f0fd16/crypto/txscript/src/opcodes/mod.rs#L1333-L1341); [covenants.rs L78-80, L107-111](https://github.com/kaspanet/rusty-kaspa/blob/01b532e8b553523216471682649693af92f0fd16/crypto/txscript/src/covenants.rs#L78-L111)). Consensus checks only the ids; what a continuation may do (script, state) is up to the covenant's own script.  **8 Oct, L1+ε ladder (Sutton):** agrees with maxibitcat's L1+ε framing ([2108272284469182499](https://x.com/michaelsuttonil/status/2108272284469182499), 19:04Z): lowest rung is bounded-size covenant state revealed at output creation (the spent cov UTXO verifies its continuation); active state size O(UTXO set), so a valid candidate for a node-level index. X, his reading; not a KIP. **10 Oct (Sutton on covenant capabilities):** [2108964596820193619](https://x.com/michaelsuttonil/status/2108964596820193619) (16:55:17Z): burn and mint are easy; freeze has tradeoffs; DEXes and lending are possible; the ingredient for compositional apps is single-transaction atomicity (onchain composability); those are the design patterns Argent and the KCCs aim at. X, his reading; not a KIP and not a status change. Build: text matches the watch's saved X raw (reply to 2108928813954453728; Build made no X call).

### Prior cell: KCC still open (to 18 Oct 2026)

Nothing below is Final except KCC-0. **KCC-1, KCC-2, and KCC-20 are Last Call, not Final.** [#32](https://github.com/kaspanet/kccs/pull/32) [`815ecaff`](https://github.com/kaspanet/kccs/commit/815ecaff) merged 1 Oct 12:33Z and [#33](https://github.com/kaspanet/kccs/pull/33) [`ad1b8996`](https://github.com/kaspanet/kccs/commit/ad1b8996) 12:52Z (michaelsutton approved and merged both). On [`411b41bc`](https://github.com/kaspanet/kccs/commit/411b41bc14b3fda8f3a0548242c555f3597cad1a), `kcc-0001.md` and `kcc-0002.md` say `Status: Last Call`. Neither header sets a `Last-Call-Deadline`, which KCC-0 requires while a KCC is in Last Call. Those two files are not in the #31 diff. `kcc-0020` is **Last Call** on main [`3fbec524`](https://github.com/kaspanet/kccs/commit/3fbec524abfbc20e87652eb938db218f8c17db17). **27 Sep 15:14Z:** [#30](https://github.com/kaspanet/kccs/pull/30) merged [`90beacd0`](https://github.com/kaspanet/kccs/commit/90beacd0dd34) (IzioDev): KCC-2 now uses unkeyed BLAKE3 for P2PKH public-key commitments, splits standard vs custom scheme ranges (`0x80`–`0xff` custom), and adds test vectors. The header was then still `Status: Draft`; #30 is not a consensus change. Before #30 the P2PKH value was keyed, `Hash(pubkey, UTF8("PublicKeyHash"))`; now it is `Hash(pubkey)` ([diff](https://github.com/kaspanet/kccs/pull/30/files)). `kcc-0020.md` on main [`3fbec524`](https://github.com/kaspanet/kccs/commit/3fbec524abfbc20e87652eb938db218f8c17db17) still writes the value as `P2PKHHash(pubkey)`, a name KCC-2 no longer defines. The two printed values are unkeyed BLAKE3: `7caa514a05535fd97887e483ce6f1fc36ef7026435c47521b04549d9af4837bf` for `22^32`, and `ed887ad164d313eeeac970912504a81156274732ab09c0c0559ff59160abddf9` for `02 || 55^32`. Borrow schemes stay exclusive bytes, not bit flags: `0x00` disabled, `0x01` amount-threshold, `0x02` schnorr-signature, `0x03` hash-chain. Any other value is invalid. A conforming program must recognize disabled and support all three enabled schemes. Default max token inputs and outputs are 3. A non-default configuration may override the entrypoints, the owner-scheme subset, and those maxima. An implementation may cap the total input token amount at `2^63-1`. That is not a supply cap. Borrowed receive is the leader only, successor `next_states[0]`. For amount-threshold, the guard is the first eight bytes, a negative decodes as zero, the increase must be strictly greater than that threshold, and the full `borrow_guard` is preserved. `Hash` in the hash-chain rule is unkeyed BLAKE3. ### Prior cell: Launch proof and binding (to 19 Oct 2026)

Sutton [2081846048280965268](https://x.com/michaelsuttonil/status/2081846048280965268) (27 Jul): every deployed L1 covenant should come with a launch proof derived from its covenant-id preimage, covering the full contracts and initial state, and with inspectable source. [2082066262520463670](https://x.com/michaelsuttonil/status/2082066262520463670) (28 Jul): the UTXO carries the covenant id (its preimage proves the launch) and the spk (p2sh commits to the contract/actor and its state). [2087453635206643755](https://x.com/michaelsuttonil/status/2087453635206643755) (12 Aug): a DEX binds each whitelisted asset by the pair (template hash, covenant id). The template is passed at runtime as an untrusted sig arg and checked against the hash. Example: [argent-playground `dex.ag` L32 at `0a2e80d1`](https://github.com/argent-lang/argent-playground/blob/0a2e80d13ac8394a62057f21db954be17bcbf994/ag/dex/dex.ag#L32). [2098077295214809214](https://x.com/michaelsuttonil/status/2098077295214809214) (10 Sep) links the formal analysis [`leader-delegate-input-groups.md`](https://github.com/argent-lang/argent/blob/master/docs/security-invariants/leader-delegate-input-groups.md) on argent master (#60, merged 10 Sep). The covenant-state provenance doc behind the silverscript#234 close is only on branch [`covenant-state-provenance`](https://github.com/argent-lang/argent/blob/covenant-state-provenance/docs/security-invariants/covenant-state-provenance.md) (`35bec64a`, 3 Sep), not on master ([Sutton](https://x.com/michaelsuttonil/status/2095472062701699101)). Sutton [2106033659698450492](https://x.com/michaelsuttonil/status/2106033659698450492) (2 Oct 14:48Z) points at [argent#66](https://github.com/argent-lang/argent/pull/66) (genesis-proof tooling, then open at head `9592dd99`) and expects every stateful covenant to publish that link. Sutton merged #66 on 4 Oct 12:04Z (14:04 CEST) as [`03d67021`](https://github.com/argent-lang/argent/commit/03d670217b7139ee452e1c50d109f600ed85d94d) (PR head `aab8fe1e`, two commits past `9592dd99`). No tag. **5 Oct, two covenant categories (Sutton):** [2107218445993738378](https://x.com/michaelsuttonil/status/2107218445993738378) (21:16Z): some covenants are about the Kaspa they protect (vaults, timelocks, escrow), others about the state they carry, which forms another mini social consensus (name services, native KCC-20 tokens). A timelock has no forgery problem, because anyone may clone the script over their own KAS; when the state itself matters, imitation does, and that is why Toccata introduced covenant ids and covenant lineage ([2107246681162948905](https://x.com/michaelsuttonil/status/2107246681162948905), 23:08Z). The genesis preimage shows the birth was right, but it matters only because the covenant id gives provable lineage ([2107241339066671607](https://x.com/michaelsuttonil/status/2107241339066671607)). A privacy pool and a based app are both kinds at once: state (notes and nullifiers; external state) plus a pool of KAS (for a based app, the canonical bridge) ([2107231201165549636](https://x.com/michaelsuttonil/status/2107231201165549636)). Native state-carrying covenants can already support assets, DEXs and lending ([2107239797513236579](https://x.com/michaelsuttonil/status/2107239797513236579)). In a separate, earlier reply (18:40Z, another conversation), P2SH also compresses: the launch of a complex app with several continuation contracts folds under 32 initial bytes ([2107179238440976510](https://x.com/michaelsuttonil/status/2107179238440976510)). On randomness ([2107237888304013388](https://x.com/michaelsuttonil/status/2107237888304013388), 22:33Z): PoW block hashes are a good source only if the mechanism cannot choose which hashes it uses; reading them from the script engine is tricky but not impossible; based apps have an easier path through the KIP-21 sequencing commitment, again without giving the mechanism or the zk prover selection power. X replies, his reading; not a KIP. In the same thread Manyfest ([2107373867396182019](https://x.com/manyfest_/status/2107373867396182019), 6 Oct 07:34Z): for the first kind the node itself checks that no KAS is created in the transition; for the second, the genesis tx creates new "matter" the node knows nothing about, so the covenant logic must enforce its conservation, and other covenants can compose on it. Asked how a user knows a contract hides no backdoor such as a `terminate()` paying the developer, Sutton answered "no doubt. hence" and quoted his 2 Oct genesis-proof post 2106033659698450492 ([2107536837522678263](https://x.com/michaelsuttonil/status/2107536837522678263), 6 Oct 18:21Z). Catalog. **Reasoning kept from a moved project:** covenant id derivation, desk recompute 3 Oct (no node) on a third-party Testnet-10 registry genesis: blake2b-256 keyed `CovenantID` over the authorizing outpoint, then each authorized output's index, value and script public key (not its covenant binding), per rusty-kaspa v2.1.0 [covenant_id.rs](https://github.com/kaspanet/rusty-kaspa/blob/01b532e8b553523216471682649693af92f0fd16/consensus/core/src/hashing/covenant_id.rs) ([hashers.rs L32](https://github.com/kaspanet/rusty-kaspa/blob/01b532e8b553523216471682649693af92f0fd16/crypto/hashes/src/hashers.rs#L32)); any change to those outputs gives a different id, and the recomputed id matched the published one. Details: see [STP-KAS/kaspa-builders](https://github.com/STP-KAS/kaspa-builders) (entry name-services). **Desk note 6 Oct, covenant lineage in rusty-kaspa v2.1.0 `01b532e8` (desk reading, not a KIP):** an output may carry covenant id X only if its authorizing input's UTXO already carries X (continuation, [covenants.rs L124-136](https://github.com/kaspanet/rusty-kaspa/blob/01b532e8b553523216471682649693af92f0fd16/crypto/txscript/src/covenants.rs#L124-L136)) or X equals the id recomputed from that input's outpoint and the group's authorized outputs (genesis, [L137-160](https://github.com/kaspanet/rusty-kaspa/blob/01b532e8b553523216471682649693af92f0fd16/crypto/txscript/src/covenants.rs#L137-L160); [covenant_id.rs L16-30](https://github.com/kaspanet/rusty-kaspa/blob/01b532e8b553523216471682649693af92f0fd16/consensus/core/src/hashing/covenant_id.rs#L16-L30)); otherwise the tx fails with `WrongGenesisCovenantId`. This runs for every tx in UTXO context ([tx_validation_in_utxo_context.rs L58](https://github.com/kaspanet/rusty-kaspa/blob/01b532e8b553523216471682649693af92f0fd16/consensus/src/processes/transaction_validator/tx_validation_in_utxo_context.rs#L58)). An outpoint is spent once, so every UTXO carrying X descends through authorizing-input links from one genesis; that is the lineage. `OpCovInputCount` (0xd0) pushes the number of tx inputs whose UTXO carries the given id ([opcodes/mod.rs L1333-1341](https://github.com/kaspanet/rusty-kaspa/blob/01b532e8b553523216471682649693af92f0fd16/crypto/txscript/src/opcodes/mod.rs#L1333-L1341); [covenants.rs L78-80, L107-111](https://github.com/kaspanet/rusty-kaspa/blob/01b532e8b553523216471682649693af92f0fd16/crypto/txscript/src/covenants.rs#L78-L111)). Consensus checks only the ids; what a continuation may do (script, state) is up to the covenant's own script.  **8 Oct, L1+ε ladder (Sutton):** agrees with maxibitcat's L1+ε framing ([2108272284469182499](https://x.com/michaelsuttonil/status/2108272284469182499), 19:04Z): lowest rung is bounded-size covenant state revealed at output creation (the spent cov UTXO verifies its continuation); active state size O(UTXO set), so a valid candidate for a node-level index. X, his reading; not a KIP. **10 Oct (Sutton on covenant capabilities):** [2108964596820193619](https://x.com/michaelsuttonil/status/2108964596820193619) (16:55:17Z): burn and mint are easy; freeze has tradeoffs; DEXes and lending are possible; the ingredient for compositional apps is single-transaction atomicity (onchain composability); those are the design patterns Argent and the KCCs aim at. X, his reading; not a KIP and not a status change. Build: text matches the watch's saved X raw (reply to 2108928813954453728; Build made no X call). **15 Oct 22:42Z (Sutton, X note; watch 16 Oct):** [2110863926527230422](https://x.com/michaelsuttonil/status/2110863926527230422) on state-carrying covenants that need lineage and a scarce global resource (name service): compressed design = one Merkle root in a single covenant UTXO (SMT over the keyspace; register proves empty slot, updates root, emits ownership UTXO `U(R₀) → U(R₁) + Point(k)`; transfers of the name need not touch the root); partitioned design = split ranges into lineage-linked covenant UTXOs so different ranges can proceed concurrently in the DAG; middle ground = fixed count of range UTXOs each with its own Merkle root. Quotes @supertypo_kas's DOTK as pure partitioning (`Gap((a,b]) → Gap((a,k)) + Deed(k) + Gap((k,b])`). KIP-9 storage mass makes many small range UTXOs expensive on purpose; expand-and-contract frontiers (as in kcc20-reference) reclaim KAS by merging. Full note saved under the watch raws. X, his reading; not a KIP. Follow-up [2110866794218950778](https://x.com/michaelsuttonil/status/2110866794218950778) points at IzioDev's SMT-based name service on fork branch `feat/name-service` (product → [kaspa-builders](https://github.com/STP-KAS/kaspa-builders) name-services entry). **Build check against the watch raw** (`x/sutton-2110863926527230422-note.txt`, 3767 bytes; no X call): the two transition lines match byte for byte (`U(R₀) → U(R₁) + Point(k)` and `Gap((a,b]) → Gap((a,k)) + Deed(k) + Gap((k,b])`). On KIP-9 the note says: "KIP-9 makes creating many small-value outputs expensive, so each new range UTXO needs enough KAS locked in it to keep the mass reasonable. That’s intentional." On the middle ground: "A practical middle ground is to start with a chosen number of range UTXOs and put a Merkle root inside each one." The saved note opens with the line "(with grok and sol)".

### Prior cell: KRC-20 incident (to 19 Oct 2026)

**Not an L1 exploit.** 20 Sep: the ZealousSwap post-mortem, as relayed by Recon [2101642546803863779](https://x.com/ReconProtocol/status/2101642546803863779), traces it to a signature bypass in the off-chain Kasplex KRC-20 indexer, not Kaspa L1. KRC-20 token state is interpreted by indexers, not by L1 consensus. Third-party report. The desk did not read the post-mortem itself. Kasplex's indexer fix release (go-krc20d) and later commits are third-party product status: kaspa-builders [entries/krc20-incident.md](https://github.com/STP-KAS/kaspa-builders/blob/main/entries/krc20-incident.md). Prior cell (to 15 Oct): [SNAPSHOT-HISTORY](SNAPSHOT-HISTORY.md#prior-cell-krc-20-incident-to-15-oct-2026).

His points: feed all key ranges to `multi_range_seek_iterator` at once instead of one query per range; take the limit before the spk filter so it tracks the actual DB iterations; bypass that filter when neither spk bound is set ("very much an expected usage pattern"); ask whether the range end should be `to_spk` and the prefix start `from_spk`; prefers tracking covenant-store sync through tips, as the utxoindex does, over the version marker (or `delete_all` when the node runs without the index); flag naming in the style of `--utxoindex`, perhaps shorter (`--covindex`); a field that may duplicate one already on `RpcUtxoEntry`; a proto field that should be optional so a blank value is None, not 0. Per-range queries: [L229](https://github.com/kaspanet/rusty-kaspa/blob/b58e51e4b5d0910d96f64a92959de4a39b3f052c/indexes/utxoindex/src/stores/indexed_utxos_by_covenant_id.rs#L229) is `.flat_map(\|key_range\| self.access.multi_range_seek_iterator(std::iter::once(key_range)))`, one seek per covenant id; the code comment at L206–L207 gives the reason, "since request order need not be ascending". Limit vs filter: the spk-bucket `.filter` (L234–L238) comes before `.take(extended_limit)` (L239), so the limit counts matching rows, not DB iterations; with no `from_spk`/`to_spk` the filter still runs and passes every row (`is_none_or`). Range bounds: the ranges start at `CovenantUtxoEntryDbKey::prefix_start(id, *daa_score_range.start())` and end at `range_end(id, *daa_score_range.end())` (L215–L220); neither uses `from_spk` or `to_spk`. In the key order (covenant id, DAA score, spk bucket, outpoint) an spk bound alone is not one contiguous range across DAA scores (Build's reading). Duplicate field: `RpcUtxosByCovenantIdsEntry` has `covenant_id: RpcHash` ([`message.rs` L1597](https://github.com/kaspanet/rusty-kaspa/blob/b58e51e4b5d0910d96f64a92959de4a39b3f052c/rpc/core/src/model/message.rs#L1597)) and holds a `RpcUtxoEntry`, which has `covenant_id: Option<RpcHash>` (`rpc/core/src/model/tx.rs`). Per-range queries: [L229](https://github.com/kaspanet/rusty-kaspa/blob/b58e51e4b5d0910d96f64a92959de4a39b3f052c/indexes/utxoindex/src/stores/indexed_utxos_by_covenant_id.rs#L229) is `.flat_map(\|key_range\| self.access.multi_range_seek_iterator(std::iter::once(key_range)))`, one seek per covenant id; the code comment at L206–L207 gives the reason, "since request order need not be ascending". Limit vs filter: the spk-bucket `.filter` (L234–L238) comes before `.take(extended_limit)` (L239), so the limit counts matching rows, not DB iterations; with no `from_spk`/`to_spk` the filter still runs and passes every row (`is_none_or`). Range bounds: the ranges start at `CovenantUtxoEntryDbKey::prefix_start(id, *daa_score_range.start())` and end at `range_end(id, *daa_score_range.end())` (L215–L220); neither uses `from_spk` or `to_spk`. In the key order (covenant id, DAA score, spk bucket, outpoint) an spk bound alone is not one contiguous range across DAA scores (Build's reading). Sync: [`invalidate_covenant_index`](https://github.com/kaspanet/rusty-kaspa/blob/b58e51e4b5d0910d96f64a92959de4a39b3f052c/indexes/utxoindex/src/stores/store_manager.rs#L188) only removes the version marker; `delete_all` runs in `reset_covenant_store`. Comments-URI is [topic 8](https://kas-smiths.org/t/fungible-token-covenant-specification-kcc20/8/). No `Last-Call-Deadline`. Not Final. Owner schemes `0x01` and `0x02` still name `P2PKHHash`. The two printed values are unkeyed BLAKE3: `7caa514a05535fd97887e483ce6f1fc36ef7026435c47521b04549d9af4837bf` for `22^32`, and `ed887ad164d313eeeac970912504a81156274732ab09c0c0559ff59160abddf9` for `02 \|\| 55^32`. Borrow schemes stay exclusive bytes, not bit flags: `0x00` disabled, `0x01` amount-threshold, `0x02` schnorr-signature, `0x03` hash-chain. Any other value is invalid. A conforming program must recognize disabled and support all three enabled schemes. Default max token inputs and outputs are 3. A non-default configuration may override the entrypoints, the owner-scheme subset, and those maxima. An implementation may cap the total input token amount at `2^63-1`. That is not a supply cap. Borrowed receive is the leader only, successor `next_states[0]`. For amount-threshold, the guard is the first eight bytes, a negative decodes as zero, the increase must be strictly greater than that threshold, and the full `borrow_guard` is preserved. `Hash` in the hash-chain rule is unkeyed BLAKE3. (3) Holds as written: [7.7](https://github.com/kaspanet/kccs/blob/8e1053ec112b7e69504f4c26cba910ec0071ea0f/kcc-0012.md#L1241-L1242) makes the version 1 (ECDSA) script spendable, [6.9](https://github.com/kaspanet/kccs/blob/8e1053ec112b7e69504f4c26cba910ec0071ea0f/kcc-0012.md#L896-L901) signs every spendable input, and [7.8](https://github.com/kaspanet/kccs/blob/8e1053ec112b7e69504f4c26cba910ec0071ea0f/kcc-0012.md#L1409-L1411) says "A wallet that acts under Section 6.9 produces `schnorr` signatures." ### Prior cell: Covenant-id lookup (to 21 Oct 2026, r2)

IzioDev [2100202631650062411](https://x.com/IzioDev/status/2100202631650062411) (16 Sep): UTXOs by covenant id "will be a future RPC endpoint". Until then, filter the UTXO set locally or use a third-party indexer. No rusty-kaspa pull for it on 28 Sep. The public Core R&D export read on 1 Oct, from 19 Aug through 1 Oct, still has no such pull. The 23-25 Sep thread is the shape of open [#991](https://github.com/kaspanet/rusty-kaspa/pull/991): no sort, no bounds, and no dedup, with the cursor as its own object. That request is not merged code. [#969](https://github.com/kaspanet/rusty-kaspa/pull/969) closed unmerged 27 Apr. [#991](https://github.com/kaspanet/rusty-kaspa/pull/991) still open. [kips.dev](https://kips.dev) and [kccs.dev](https://kccs.dev) are IzioDev mirrors synced every 24h ([2093118560822297060](https://x.com/IzioDev/status/2093118560822297060)); mirrors, not the source. Third-party indexers and tooling until that endpoint exists (kascov, [ChainAgnostic/namespaces#193](https://github.com/ChainAgnostic/namespaces/pull/193)): see [STP-KAS/kaspa-builders](https://github.com/STP-KAS/kaspa-builders). elldeeone [`rk-with-tcp`](https://github.com/elldeeone/rusty-kaspa/tree/rk-with-tcp) (`09fc0ba5`, 25 Aug) is a rusty-kaspa fork branch for inbound links between private nodes ([post](https://x.com/elldeeone/status/2085199203903721856)); no upstream pull. 14 Oct: at master 67686482 the wallet generator skips UTXOs with a covenant id (`get_utxo_entry`). That is wallet selection, not the RPC. The endpoint is still not on master. Prior cell (to 14 Oct): [SNAPSHOT-HISTORY](SNAPSHOT-HISTORY.md#prior-cell-covenant-id-lookup-to-14-oct-2026). **17 Oct (watch):** a pull now exists: [#1152](https://github.com/kaspanet/rusty-kaspa/pull/1152) "UtxoIndex: covenant id index, adds paginated GetUtxosByCovenantIds RPC" by biryukovmaxim, opened 16 Oct 11:54:21Z on `master`, head [`b58e51e4`](https://github.com/kaspanet/rusty-kaspa/commit/b58e51e4b5d0910d96f64a92959de4a39b3f052c), 42 files (+2051/−62); open, no reviews, no comments (API read 17 Oct ~05:41Z). Per the PR body: exact current-covenant-id match (UTXOs with no covenant id are not indexed), a secondary store in the utxoindex database (prefixes 196/197, its own version marker, backfilled from the address store on the first enabled start), and a paginated `GetUtxosByCovenantIds` RPC that mirrors `GetUtxosByAddressesV2` (5000 page size and 5000 ids at most, default 1000; more needs `--unsaferpc`); no notifications. Borrow schemes stay exclusive bytes, not bit flags: `0x00` disabled, `0x01` amount-threshold, `0x02` schnorr-signature, `0x03` hash-chain. Any other value is invalid. A conforming program must recognize disabled and support all three enabled schemes. Default max token inputs and outputs are 3. A non-default configuration may override the entrypoints, the owner-scheme subset, and those maxima. An implementation may cap the total input token amount at `2^63-1`. That is not a supply cap. Borrowed receive is the leader only, successor `next_states[0]`. For amount-threshold, the guard is the first eight bytes, a negative decodes as zero, the increase must be strictly greater than that threshold, and the full `borrow_guard` is preserved. `Hash` in the hash-chain rule is unkeyed BLAKE3. ### Prior cell: KCC-3/4/5 (to 21 Oct 2026, r2)

**Not on main.** [#29](https://github.com/kaspanet/kccs/pull/29) (`55742861`, kaspahttp402, 21 Sep) proposes Draft **Reputation Deed / Slashable Bond / Deed Identity Registry** as KCC 3, 4, and 5. ### Prior cell: KCC-20 wording (to 21 Oct 2026, KCC-20 Final)

Michael Sutton, [20 Sep](https://x.com/michaelsuttonil/status/2101641365419417797): a properly written KCC-20 covenant gets L1 enforcement of those rules; KCC-20 itself is a spec. One buggy instance is not a verdict on the script engine, and it is not “KCC-20 shipped.” Same morning he separated KRC-20 (off-chain interpretation) from covenants. Catalog, not a status change. The file is **Last Call** on main [`3fbec524`](https://github.com/kaspanet/kccs/commit/3fbec524abfbc20e87652eb938db218f8c17db17) since [#31](https://github.com/kaspanet/kccs/pull/31) (7 Oct 20:38Z), not Final. **11 Oct, KRC-20 to KCC-20 migration (Sutton's statement):** replying to GabrielNico21 ([2109049463302156773](https://x.com/GabrielNico21/status/2109049463302156773), 10 Oct 22:32:30Z), who asked whether a token can still migrate to KCC20 if its KRC-20 minting is unfinished, Sutton ([2109305350008475670](https://x.com/michaelsuttonil/status/2109305350008475670), 11 Oct 15:29:19Z / 17:29:19 CEST) wrote: "yes it can migrate with the same rules. it will need a custom migration with the target KCC-20 contracts supporting the same public minting policy over the remaining supply. (my answer is not specific to some migration proposed by specific entities which i know nothing about; it’s about the conceptual question)" **11 Oct, KCC-20 vs Solana (Sutton's statement):** HuseyinSivridag asked ([2109311950651834538](https://x.com/HuseyinSivridag/status/2109311950651834538), 15:55:32Z / 17:55:32 CEST): "Will the Kcc20 smart contract language possess the full smart contract capabilities of Solana?" Sutton replied ([2109315001034875348](https://x.com/michaelsuttonil/status/2109315001034875348), 16:07:40Z / 18:07:40 CEST), full text: "not easily, no. a solana program has more capabilities and can be longer and more expressive. sophisticated designs can create a multi-contract argent app that executes complex behavior across partitioned state and over multiple transactions (that’s why i called these “mini programs”), like i did with chess, but then composition with other covenants/apps needs to be carefully designed, as does contention over shared variables/state.<br>in short, i cannot promise you yet that things will run smoothly and compose cleanly. we are not a solana vm by design, and hence i expect the created apps/systems to be shaped differently to match the inherent constraints. so i can’t promise how exactly this will evolve, but my strong hypothesis is that it enables significantly complicated systems.<br>(the answer above is all within pure covenants and does not talk about based zk apps, which are as fully expressive as a solana program but currently have limited L1 composability that depends on zk proof submission)" His follow-up ([2109316491417878839](https://x.com/michaelsuttonil/status/2109316491417878839), 16:13:35Z / 18:13:35 CEST) is only a link to a [Grok share](https://x.com/i/grok/share/c2hhcmQtMw_fffeb959-8edf-4095-a5e0-2b7aa514d983); its content was not read here, so it is not described. The earlier post where he called them "mini programs" is not in this file. Desk reading, hedged, not his words: his answer is "not easily, no"; he says a Solana program has more capabilities and can be longer and more expressive, and that sophisticated designs can split an Argent app across several contracts, partitioned state and multiple transactions; he does not promise clean composition, but states a "strong hypothesis" that it enables significantly complicated systems; the answer covers pure covenants only, and he calls based ZK apps as fully expressive as a Solana program but with limited L1 composability today. Chess is his example, not desk-checked. Prior cell: [SNAPSHOT-HISTORY](SNAPSHOT-HISTORY.md#now-row-kcc-20-wording-as-of-11-oct-2026-before-the-sutton-solana-rewrite). **Cross-links (11 Oct):** the migration reply goes with the KRC-20 to KCC row (Sutton's 19 Aug snapshot preference, manyfest's proposal). The two printed values are unkeyed BLAKE3: `7caa514a05535fd97887e483ce6f1fc36ef7026435c47521b04549d9af4837bf` for `22^32`, and `ed887ad164d313eeeac970912504a81156274732ab09c0c0559ff59160abddf9` for `02 \|\| 55^32`. Borrow schemes stay exclusive bytes, not bit flags: `0x00` disabled, `0x01` amount-threshold, `0x02` schnorr-signature, `0x03` hash-chain. Any other value is invalid. A conforming program must recognize disabled and support all three enabled schemes. Default max token inputs and outputs are 3. A non-default configuration may override the entrypoints, the owner-scheme subset, and those maxima. An implementation may cap the total input token amount at `2^63-1`. That is not a supply cap. Borrowed receive is the leader only, successor `next_states[0]`. For amount-threshold, the guard is the first eight bytes, a negative decodes as zero, the increase must be strictly greater than that threshold, and the full `borrow_guard` is preserved. `Hash` in the hash-chain rule is unkeyed BLAKE3. The vector block prints dispatch tags `79c71c23` and `fd3ef14a`. Reference Implementation links [argent-lang/kcc20-reference](https://github.com/argent-lang/kcc20-reference). KCC-0 §4 says a Standards Track KCC moves to Final only when "every entry in `Requires` is itself Final (for KCCs) or Active (for KIPs)". So KCC-20 (`Requires: KCC-1, KCC-2, KIP-20`) cannot go Final while KCC-1 is Last Call. The same rule applies to KCC-2 itself: its header says `Requires: KCC-1, KIP-20`, yet it was merged as Final while KCC-1 is still Last Call. On the file text, KCC-2's Final status does not meet criterion 3. This is a reading of KCC-0, not a ruling.

The owner key reclaims the KAS: `reclaim` requires `remaining == 0` and `checkSig`, and `reclaim_into` lets the survivor lead with no signature while the retiring owner signs `reclaim_delegator`. `TokenSeed.create` requires amount zero. It builds a receiving UTXO. The supply comes from `mint`. Seed `split` is permissionless and has no half cap. Seed `reclaim` consumes a retiring seed and recreates the leader, so a lone seed has no reclaim. The lifecycle test `minter_split_mint_and_reclaim_return_unused_allowance` builds the split with no signature, rejects `take` 13 from remaining 25, and accepts `take` 7. ### Prior cell: Covenant-id lookup (to 23 Oct 2026)

IzioDev [2100202631650062411](https://x.com/IzioDev/status/2100202631650062411) (16 Sep): UTXOs by covenant id "will be a future RPC endpoint". Until then, filter the UTXO set locally or use a third-party indexer. No rusty-kaspa pull for it on 28 Sep. The public Core R&D export read on 1 Oct, from 19 Aug through 1 Oct, still has no such pull. The 23-25 Sep thread is the shape of open [#991](https://github.com/kaspanet/rusty-kaspa/pull/991): no sort, no bounds, and no dedup, with the cursor as its own object. That request is not merged code. [#969](https://github.com/kaspanet/rusty-kaspa/pull/969) closed unmerged 27 Apr. [#991](https://github.com/kaspanet/rusty-kaspa/pull/991) still open. [kips.dev](https://kips.dev) and [kccs.dev](https://kccs.dev) are IzioDev mirrors synced every 24h ([2093118560822297060](https://x.com/IzioDev/status/2093118560822297060)); mirrors, not the source. Third-party indexers and tooling until that endpoint exists (kascov, [ChainAgnostic/namespaces#193](https://github.com/ChainAgnostic/namespaces/pull/193)): see [STP-KAS/kaspa-builders](https://github.com/STP-KAS/kaspa-builders). elldeeone [`rk-with-tcp`](https://github.com/elldeeone/rusty-kaspa/tree/rk-with-tcp) (`09fc0ba5`, 25 Aug) is a rusty-kaspa fork branch for inbound links between private nodes ([post](https://x.com/elldeeone/status/2085199203903721856)); no upstream pull. 14 Oct: at master 67686482 the wallet generator skips UTXOs with a covenant id (`get_utxo_entry`). That is wallet selection, not the RPC. The endpoint is still not on master. Prior cell (to 14 Oct): [SNAPSHOT-HISTORY](SNAPSHOT-HISTORY.md#prior-cell-covenant-id-lookup-to-14-oct-2026). **17 Oct (watch):** a pull now exists: [#1152](https://github.com/kaspanet/rusty-kaspa/pull/1152) "UtxoIndex: covenant id index, adds paginated GetUtxosByCovenantIds RPC" by biryukovmaxim, opened 16 Oct 11:54:21Z on `master`, head [`b58e51e4`](https://github.com/kaspanet/rusty-kaspa/commit/b58e51e4b5d0910d96f64a92959de4a39b3f052c), 42 files (+2051/−62); open, no reviews, no comments (API read 17 Oct ~05:41Z). Per the PR body: exact current-covenant-id match (UTXOs with no covenant id are not indexed), a secondary store in the utxoindex database (prefixes 196/197, its own version marker, backfilled from the address store on the first enabled start), and a paginated `GetUtxosByCovenantIds` RPC that mirrors `GetUtxosByAddressesV2` (5000 page size and 5000 ids at most, default 1000; more needs `--unsaferpc`); no notifications. Proposed code, unreviewed, not desk-built. The endpoint is still not on master. D-Stacks left 10 inline review comments on head `b58e51e4` (10 reviews, all COMMENTED, 18 Oct 13:04:21Z to 17:52:28Z; no approval, no change request). His points: feed all key ranges to `multi_range_seek_iterator` at once instead of one query per range; take the limit before the spk filter so it tracks the actual DB iterations; bypass that filter when neither spk bound is set ("very much an expected usage pattern"); ask whether the range end should be `to_spk` and the prefix start `from_spk`; prefers tracking covenant-store sync through tips, as the utxoindex does, over the version marker (or `delete_all` when the node runs without the index); flag naming in the style of `--utxoindex`, perhaps shorter (`--covindex`); a field that may duplicate one already on `RpcUtxoEntry`; a proto field that should be optional so a blank value is None, not 0. Still a **draft**, `mergeable_state` behind, 0 issue comments. Review comments, not a merge decision; the endpoint is still not on master `f7d78773`. Prior cell (to 19 Oct): [SNAPSHOT-HISTORY](https://github.com/STP-KAS/kaspa-master-file/blob/main/SNAPSHOT-HISTORY.md#prior-cell-covenant-id-lookup-to-19-oct-2026). **Build check of the 10 inline comments against [`b58e51e4`](https://github.com/kaspanet/rusty-kaspa/commit/b58e51e4b5d0910d96f64a92959de4a39b3f052c) (every page: 10 reviews, all COMMENTED; 10 review comments; 0 issue comments):** each point describes the code as written. Per-range queries: [L229](https://github.com/kaspanet/rusty-kaspa/blob/b58e51e4b5d0910d96f64a92959de4a39b3f052c/indexes/utxoindex/src/stores/indexed_utxos_by_covenant_id.rs#L229) is `.flat_map(\|key_range\| self.access.multi_range_seek_iterator(std::iter::once(key_range)))`, one seek per covenant id; the code comment at L206–L207 gives the reason, "since request order need not be ascending". Limit vs filter: the spk-bucket `.filter` (L234–L238) comes before `.take(extended_limit)` (L239), so the limit counts matching rows, not DB iterations; with no `from_spk`/`to_spk` the filter still runs and passes every row (`is_none_or`). Range bounds: the ranges start at `CovenantUtxoEntryDbKey::prefix_start(id, *daa_score_range.start())` and end at `range_end(id, *daa_score_range.end())` (L215–L220); neither uses `from_spk` or `to_spk`. Sync: [`invalidate_covenant_index`](https://github.com/kaspanet/rusty-kaspa/blob/b58e51e4b5d0910d96f64a92959de4a39b3f052c/indexes/utxoindex/src/stores/store_manager.rs#L188) only removes the version marker; `delete_all` runs in `reset_covenant_store`. Flag: `Arg::new("covenant-index")` next to `--utxoindex` in [`kaspad/src/args.rs` L353](https://github.com/kaspanet/rusty-kaspa/blob/b58e51e4b5d0910d96f64a92959de4a39b3f052c/kaspad/src/args.rs#L353). Duplicate field: `RpcUtxosByCovenantIdsEntry` has `covenant_id: RpcHash` ([`message.rs` L1597](https://github.com/kaspanet/rusty-kaspa/blob/b58e51e4b5d0910d96f64a92959de4a39b3f052c/rpc/core/src/model/message.rs#L1597)) and holds a `RpcUtxoEntry`, which has `covenant_id: Option<RpcHash>` (`rpc/core/src/model/tx.rs`). Proto: `uint64 startDaaScore = 2;` is not `optional` ([`rpc.proto` L625](https://github.com/kaspanet/rusty-kaspa/blob/b58e51e4b5d0910d96f64a92959de4a39b3f052c/rpc/grpc/core/proto/rpc.proto#L625)), while its siblings are. He calls this reference the first step toward a general standardized Kaspa Token Lib (KTL), or more broadly non-token contracts and libs. X, his reading; not a KIP. **Supply caps:** KCC-20 alone sets no cap. IzioDev [2103117174176878937](https://x.com/IzioDev/status/2103117174176878937) (24 Sep): a cap lives in a minter covenant on top; trusting a token means verifying its genesis and auditing the sources. Forging is blocked by the consensus covenant lineage rule; forking into several UTXOs with the same covenant_id is allowed ([2103434848593457558](https://x.com/IzioDev/status/2103434848593457558), 25 Sep). `public_mint.ag` at `8c8dc8ee` is such a minter, and `split` can move allowance onto another deposit in the same family. One mint is one transaction. One minter output can be spent only once at a time, so parallel minting first needs a split tree; `split` adds one minter per call, so 5,000 leaves need 4,999 splits (arithmetic). **TN10 desk run, 11 Oct** (stp's desk; public repo, [stp-trump2028 `map/bot/FINDINGS.md`](https://github.com/STP-KAS/stp-trump2028/blob/15cbdcbc8b7642cb8e689e4934881e16b5379058/map/bot/FINDINGS.md) at `15cbdcbc`): 2,488 public mints with this app at `c8a08711` through one local node, 2,488 accepted, 0 rejected ([`mints.json`](https://github.com/STP-KAS/stp-trump2028/blob/15cbdcbc8b7642cb8e689e4934881e16b5379058/map/bot/mints.json) lists 2,488); per mint compute mass 9,117, transient 26,068, storage 61,710 to 76,586 grams with a 1 tKAS carrier; 204 sompi/gram, 0.126 to 0.156 tKAS per mint (61,710 and 76,586 grams × 204 sompi match that range); fees 322.74917112 tKAS in total. A settlement from a fragmented funder wallet (37 small UTXOs) exceeded the per-tx mass cap (516,168 > 500,000); the node rejected it; the settler's unrecoverable stop took the daemon down; unflushed receipts were lost; on restart the committed-gap pass treated the miss as terminal and froze the covenant. Fixes: flush receipts with the durability latch; bound the funding walk by the mass cap; back off on a mass-capped dead-end; and (on the same stack) #170. In `consensus/src/model/stores/utxo_set.rs`, a new `UtxoImportWriter` buffers writes in one RocksDB `WriteBatch` and writes it to the DB when it reaches 1000 entries or 1 MiB (`1 << 20` bytes), and once more at the end of each call. It is used only by two new IBD methods: `write_imported_chunk` (pruning-point import, from `consensus/mod.rs`) and `copy_imported_from_iterator` (copy into virtual, from `virtual_processor/processor.rs`). Ordinary UTXO writes keep their writer. `utxo_set/import_tests.rs` checks that batched imports give the same rows as direct writes, including last-write-wins across a batch boundary, and that the copy path updates the cache. It also checks that the writer flushes at the entry and byte bounds and keeps the tail until the final flush. A third disk benchmark test is `#[ignore]`. ### Prior cell: Covenant-id lookup (to 26 Oct 2026)

IzioDev [2100202631650062411](https://x.com/IzioDev/status/2100202631650062411) (16 Sep): UTXOs by covenant id "will be a future RPC endpoint". Until then, filter the UTXO set locally or use a third-party indexer. No rusty-kaspa pull for it on 28 Sep. The public Core R&D export read on 1 Oct, from 19 Aug through 1 Oct, still has no such pull. The 23-25 Sep thread is the shape of open [#991](https://github.com/kaspanet/rusty-kaspa/pull/991): no sort, no bounds, and no dedup, with the cursor as its own object. That request is not merged code. [#969](https://github.com/kaspanet/rusty-kaspa/pull/969) closed unmerged 27 Apr. [#991](https://github.com/kaspanet/rusty-kaspa/pull/991) still open. [kips.dev](https://kips.dev) and [kccs.dev](https://kccs.dev) are IzioDev mirrors synced every 24h ([2093118560822297060](https://x.com/IzioDev/status/2093118560822297060)); mirrors, not the source. Third-party indexers and tooling until that endpoint exists (kascov, [ChainAgnostic/namespaces#193](https://github.com/ChainAgnostic/namespaces/pull/193)): see [STP-KAS/kaspa-builders](https://github.com/STP-KAS/kaspa-builders). elldeeone [`rk-with-tcp`](https://github.com/elldeeone/rusty-kaspa/tree/rk-with-tcp) (`09fc0ba5`, 25 Aug) is a rusty-kaspa fork branch for inbound links between private nodes ([post](https://x.com/elldeeone/status/2085199203903721856)); no upstream pull. 14 Oct: at master 67686482 the wallet generator skips UTXOs with a covenant id (`get_utxo_entry`). That is wallet selection, not the RPC. The endpoint is still not on master. Prior cell (to 14 Oct): [SNAPSHOT-HISTORY](SNAPSHOT-HISTORY.md#prior-cell-covenant-id-lookup-to-14-oct-2026). **17 Oct (watch):** a pull now exists: [#1152](https://github.com/kaspanet/rusty-kaspa/pull/1152) "UtxoIndex: covenant id index, adds paginated GetUtxosByCovenantIds RPC" by biryukovmaxim, opened 16 Oct 11:54:21Z on `master`, head [`b58e51e4`](https://github.com/kaspanet/rusty-kaspa/commit/b58e51e4b5d0910d96f64a92959de4a39b3f052c), 42 files (+2051/−62); open, no reviews, no comments (API read 17 Oct ~05:41Z). Per the PR body: exact current-covenant-id match (UTXOs with no covenant id are not indexed), a secondary store in the utxoindex database (prefixes 196/197, its own version marker, backfilled from the address store on the first enabled start), and a paginated `GetUtxosByCovenantIds` RPC that mirrors `GetUtxosByAddressesV2` (5000 page size and 5000 ids at most, default 1000; more needs `--unsaferpc`); no notifications. Proposed code, unreviewed, not desk-built. The endpoint is still not on master. D-Stacks left 10 inline review comments on head `b58e51e4` (10 reviews, all COMMENTED, 18 Oct 13:04:21Z to 17:52:28Z; no approval, no change request). His points: feed all key ranges to `multi_range_seek_iterator` at once instead of one query per range; take the limit before the spk filter so it tracks the actual DB iterations; bypass that filter when neither spk bound is set ("very much an expected usage pattern"); ask whether the range end should be `to_spk` and the prefix start `from_spk`; prefers tracking covenant-store sync through tips, as the utxoindex does, over the version marker (or `delete_all` when the node runs without the index); flag naming in the style of `--utxoindex`, perhaps shorter (`--covindex`); a field that may duplicate one already on `RpcUtxoEntry`; a proto field that should be optional so a blank value is None, not 0. Still a **draft**, `mergeable_state` behind, 0 issue comments. Review comments, not a merge decision; the endpoint is still not on master `f7d78773`. A settlement from a fragmented funder wallet (37 small UTXOs) exceeded the per-tx mass cap (516,168 > 500,000); the node rejected it; the settler's unrecoverable stop took the daemon down; unflushed receipts were lost; on restart the committed-gap pass treated the miss as terminal and froze the covenant. Fixes: flush receipts with the durability latch; bound the funding walk by the mass cap; back off on a mass-capped dead-end; and (on the same stack) #170. In the playground's `multiapp_badge`, `Badge.apply` trusts any co-spend of its controller ([badge_asset.ag L10](https://github.com/argent-lang/argent-playground/blob/908c0a7ec6102ff062e77fbcc6c54e780f3f4e52/ag/multiapp_badge/badge_asset.ag#L10)) while `Controller.mint` observes only the badge it selects ([badge_controller.ag L8-9](https://github.com/argent-lang/argent-playground/blob/908c0a7ec6102ff062e77fbcc6c54e780f3f4e52/ag/multiapp_badge/badge_controller.ag#L8-L9)); **18 Oct (watch):** [#71](https://github.com/argent-lang/argent/pull/71) "Build against rusty-kaspa v2.1.0 and silverscript 1.0.1" was opened 18 Oct 01:13:33Z by [Silentpartnercoding](https://github.com/Silentpartnercoding) from a fork (head `187e462e`, 1 commit, 3 files, +68/−36, not draft, `mergeable_state` blocked, no review). #### Prior master.json note: Argent (to 26 Oct 2026)

Master 9a9f4b107116d0b259fae629f200fa3b663e7e9d (7 Oct 08:24Z): Sutton merged #68 https://github.com/argent-lang/argent/pull/68 (opened 6 Oct 15:05Z, head 1aa055c3, no review): the current actor's template lengths become fixed-width byte[4] constants filled in one pass, replacing hidden length arguments; foreign template witnesses unchanged; 6 files at merge. Per the PR diff of artifact.json (not compiled here), the stones Player template's sil_template_hash and the artifact id change (7133efc5... to e843bab4...). Open #69 https://github.com/argent-lang/argent/pull/69 (RossKU, 8 Oct 14:52Z, no review): import "./asset/artifact.json" id "<artifact id>"; would link a published app artifact without its source. 8 Oct, Ross Ku (third-party, not desk-checked): his notes at RossKU/kob 9d8030c9 https://github.com/RossKU/kob/blob/9d8030c9b1aca370af2315230c15920c021e39a2/docs/argent-feedback.md say that with an artifact import the interface fingerprint excludes the handle, so whoever supplies the artifact chooses which template the importer accepts, and his item 12 patch for that pin is open #69 (head 435fa89ae4e717e0e8df627e36f372cc106c1bab on RossKU/argent, 9 files, no review, not merged; argent master still 9a9f4b10 on 9 Oct 06:37Z). The rest of his 8 Oct material is in kaspa-builders https://github.com/STP-KAS/kaspa-builders/blob/main/entries/rossku-kob.md#argent-port-notes-8-oct-2026 (third-party, not desk-checked). Before #68, master 232c6ee621107846e81146f853034464f811db15 (5 Oct 11:48Z, the #67 merge, Sutton) https://github.com/argent-lang/argent/pull/67 : id.co_spent() was lowered to an unparenthesized OpCovInputCount(id) > 0, so !id.co_spent() negated the count, not the boolean (the PR's description); every generated co-spend comparison is now parenthesized. Per the PR: 549 tests pass; generated Sil pins gain parentheses; existing compiled scripts, template hashes and artifacts unchanged (not desk-checked). Same day, demo argent-playground#7 908c0a7ec6102ff062e77fbcc6c54e780f3f4e52 (12:27Z) https://github.com/argent-lang/argent-playground/pull/7 : DEX move_reserve now requires the other reserve asset's covenant to be absent (require(!base_id.co_spent()) / require(!quote_id.co_spent())); before, an extra input could move the other reserve in the same tx. The PR calls the DEX a demo with no security guarantees. No tag. Before #67, 03d670217b7139ee452e1c50d109f600ed85d94d (4 Oct 12:04Z, the #66 merge). Before that, b312deda6fe10f6493c8d49eb748e3f61860458a (30 Sep 11:10Z), two commits after #62 7008e59b (29 Sep 07:15Z): #65 5301fe15b762e580b7c89d0d54169f0ac2b50191 (29 Sep 22:05Z) is a multi-actor README example, and b312deda refreshes the status paragraph. https://github.com/argent-lang/argent/commit/b312deda6fe10f6493c8d49eb748e3f61860458a. The README says not release-ready, pinned to SilverScript v1.0.0, and careful early use only if the generated sil is reviewed. That sentence is not a tag and not general production. Tags API returned empty on 1 Oct. #62 still stands: module imports with optional aliases, per-module name resolution, ambiguous references rejected. 1 Oct public Core R&D: Sutton answered Ross Ku. Ross Ku notes https://t.me/kasparnd/16113 (29 Sep 22:56Z): router 25-35 KB (a cancel ~0.05-0.07 KAS on TN10), split into one actor per shape (2.4-8.5 KB); a naive two-order tx let the builder keep ~10 KAS when one output satisfied both orders; he added a positional payout rule (his figures; not observed by the desk). IzioDev https://t.me/kasparnd/16114 (30 Sep 02:38Z): points 1 and 2 (co_spent gating, an entry with no become) are as designed. KOB is a hand-written SilverScript order book with Argent outside it. No repo is named. co_spent is a presence check. The acting actor must become on every branch. An observed covenant's outputs stay that contract's job. Output aliasing is application logic. Observed ranges are planned before the first release. Per-entry script splitting is not in that release. A nested KCC-20 changes the surrounding template. actor_type_handle is the stable KCC-1 view. ### Prior cell: KCC-20 wording (to 27 Oct 2026)

Michael Sutton, [20 Sep](https://x.com/michaelsuttonil/status/2101641365419417797): a properly written KCC-20 covenant gets L1 enforcement of those rules; KCC-20 itself is a spec. One buggy instance is not a verdict on the script engine, and it is not “KCC-20 shipped.” Same morning he separated KRC-20 (off-chain interpretation) from covenants. The file is **Last Call** on main [`3fbec524`](https://github.com/kaspanet/kccs/commit/3fbec524abfbc20e87652eb938db218f8c17db17) since [#31](https://github.com/kaspanet/kccs/pull/31) (7 Oct 20:38Z), not Final. **11 Oct, KRC-20 to KCC-20 migration (Sutton's statement):** replying to GabrielNico21 ([2109049463302156773](https://x.com/GabrielNico21/status/2109049463302156773), 10 Oct 22:32:30Z), who asked whether a token can still migrate to KCC20 if its KRC-20 minting is unfinished, Sutton ([2109305350008475670](https://x.com/michaelsuttonil/status/2109305350008475670), 11 Oct 15:29:19Z / 17:29:19 CEST) wrote: "yes it can migrate with the same rules. it will need a custom migration with the target KCC-20 contracts supporting the same public minting policy over the remaining supply. (my answer is not specific to some migration proposed by specific entities which i know nothing about; it’s about the conceptual question)" **11 Oct, KCC-20 vs Solana (Sutton's statement):** HuseyinSivridag asked ([2109311950651834538](https://x.com/HuseyinSivridag/status/2109311950651834538), 15:55:32Z / 17:55:32 CEST): "Will the Kcc20 smart contract language possess the full smart contract capabilities of Solana?" Sutton replied ([2109315001034875348](https://x.com/michaelsuttonil/status/2109315001034875348), 16:07:40Z / 18:07:40 CEST), full text: "not easily, no. a solana program has more capabilities and can be longer and more expressive. sophisticated designs can create a multi-contract argent app that executes complex behavior across partitioned state and over multiple transactions (that’s why i called these “mini programs”), like i did with chess, but then composition with other covenants/apps needs to be carefully designed, as does contention over shared variables/state.<br>in short, i cannot promise you yet that things will run smoothly and compose cleanly. we are not a solana vm by design, and hence i expect the created apps/systems to be shaped differently to match the inherent constraints. so i can’t promise how exactly this will evolve, but my strong hypothesis is that it enables significantly complicated systems.<br>(the answer above is all within pure covenants and does not talk about based zk apps, which are as fully expressive as a solana program but currently have limited L1 composability that depends on zk proof submission)" His follow-up ([2109316491417878839](https://x.com/michaelsuttonil/status/2109316491417878839), 16:13:35Z / 18:13:35 CEST) is only a link to a [Grok share](https://x.com/i/grok/share/c2hhcmQtMw_fffeb959-8edf-4095-a5e0-2b7aa514d983); its content was not read here, so it is not described. The earlier post where he called them "mini programs" is not in this file. he says a Solana program has more capabilities and can be longer and more expressive, and that sophisticated designs can split an Argent app across several contracts, partitioned state and multiple transactions; he does not promise clean composition, but states a "strong hypothesis" that it enables significantly complicated systems; the answer covers pure covenants only, and he calls based ZK apps as fully expressive as a Solana program but with limited L1 composability today. Chess is his example, not desk-checked. Prior cell: [SNAPSHOT-HISTORY](SNAPSHOT-HISTORY.md#now-row-kcc-20-wording-as-of-11-oct-2026-before-the-sutton-solana-rewrite). **Cross-links (11 Oct):** the migration reply goes with the KRC-20 to KCC row (Sutton's 19 Aug snapshot preference, manyfest's proposal). His "contention over shared variables/state" is the open question of Kas-Smiths topic [160](https://kas-smiths.org/t/high-bps-covenant-state-pressure-utxo-contention-storage-mass-and-settlement-frequency-seeking-corrections/160) (weirdtualguy, 9 Oct 20:42Z: covenant UTXO contention, storage mass at 10 BPS, MEV; 1 post, no replies at the 11 Oct 17:13Z read); see Kas-Smiths. The two printed values are unkeyed BLAKE3: `7caa514a05535fd97887e483ce6f1fc36ef7026435c47521b04549d9af4837bf` for `22^32`, and `ed887ad164d313eeeac970912504a81156274732ab09c0c0559ff59160abddf9` for `02 \|\| 55^32`. Borrow schemes stay exclusive bytes, not bit flags: `0x00` disabled, `0x01` amount-threshold, `0x02` schnorr-signature, `0x03` hash-chain. Any other value is invalid. A conforming program must recognize disabled and support all three enabled schemes. Default max token inputs and outputs are 3. A non-default configuration may override the entrypoints, the owner-scheme subset, and those maxima. An implementation may cap the total input token amount at `2^63-1`. That is not a supply cap. Borrowed receive is the leader only, successor `next_states[0]`. For amount-threshold, the guard is the first eight bytes, a negative decodes as zero, the increase must be strictly greater than that threshold, and the full `borrow_guard` is preserved. `Hash` in the hash-chain rule is unkeyed BLAKE3. The vector block prints dispatch tags `79c71c23` and `fd3ef14a`. Reference Implementation links [argent-lang/kcc20-reference](https://github.com/argent-lang/kcc20-reference). #### Prior master.json note: Sutton on KCC-20 (to 27 Oct 2026)

20 Sep 2026. A properly written KCC-20 covenant is enforced by L1. KCC-20 is still a spec. One buggy instance is not a verdict on the script engine. Same morning: KRC-20 state is off-chain interpretation, not L1. Catalog. The file is Last Call on kccs main 3fbec524 since #31 (2026-10-07T20:38:09Z), not Final. 11 Oct, KRC-20 to KCC-20 migration (Sutton's statement): replying to GabrielNico21 (2109049463302156773 https://x.com/GabrielNico21/status/2109049463302156773, 10 Oct 22:32:30Z), who asked whether a token can still migrate to KCC20 if its KRC-20 minting is unfinished, Sutton (2109305350008475670 https://x.com/michaelsuttonil/status/2109305350008475670, 11 Oct 15:29:19Z / 17:29:19 CEST) wrote: "yes it can migrate with the same rules. it will need a custom migration with the target KCC-20 contracts supporting the same public minting policy over the remaining supply. (my answer is not specific to some migration proposed by specific entities which i know nothing about; it’s about the conceptual question)" 11 Oct, KCC-20 vs Solana (Sutton's statement): HuseyinSivridag asked (2109311950651834538 https://x.com/HuseyinSivridag/status/2109311950651834538, 15:55:32Z / 17:55:32 CEST): "Will the Kcc20 smart contract language possess the full smart contract capabilities of Solana?" Sutton replied (2109315001034875348 https://x.com/michaelsuttonil/status/2109315001034875348, 16:07:40Z / 18:07:40 CEST), full text: "not easily, no. a solana program has more capabilities and can be longer and more expressive. sophisticated designs can create a multi-contract argent app that executes complex behavior across partitioned state and over multiple transactions (that’s why i called these “mini programs”), like i did with chess, but then composition with other covenants/apps needs to be carefully designed, as does contention over shared variables/state.
in short, i cannot promise you yet that things will run smoothly and compose cleanly. we are not a solana vm by design, and hence i expect the created apps/systems to be shaped differently to match the inherent constraints. so i can’t promise how exactly this will evolve, but my strong hypothesis is that it enables significantly complicated systems.
(the answer above is all within pure covenants and does not talk about based zk apps, which are as fully expressive as a solana program but currently have limited L1 composability that depends on zk proof submission)" His follow-up (2109316491417878839 https://x.com/michaelsuttonil/status/2109316491417878839, 16:13:35Z / 18:13:35 CEST) is only a link to a Grok share https://x.com/i/grok/share/c2hhcmQtMw_fffeb959-8edf-4095-a5e0-2b7aa514d983; its content was not read here, so it is not described. The earlier post where he called them "mini programs" is not in this file. he says a Solana program has more capabilities and can be longer and more expressive, and that sophisticated designs can split an Argent app across several contracts, partitioned state and multiple transactions; he does not promise clean composition, but states a "strong hypothesis" that it enables significantly complicated systems; the answer covers pure covenants only, and he calls based ZK apps as fully expressive as a Solana program but with limited L1 composability today. Chess is his example, not desk-checked. ### Prior cell: 26–30 Sep notes (to 29 Oct 2026)

rusty-kaspa [#1140](https://github.com/kaspanet/rusty-kaspa/issues/1140) (30 Sep, SDK v2.1.0 findings from mainnet) is still open. atharaldsen [reproduced item 1](https://github.com/kaspanet/rusty-kaspa/issues/1140#issuecomment-5983592399) (4 Oct 19:30Z) on master with testnet-10 params: one 100 KAS UTXO, `priorityFee` 0, one output of input − 0.002 gives `Storage mass exceeds maximum`; any `feeRate` makes it pass. His cause: `Generator::calculate_mass` keeps the tiny change because without a fee rate the storage mass of the change never enters the keep-vs-absorb test. He points to IzioDev's open [#894](https://github.com/kaspanet/rusty-kaspa/pull/894) (head `ad72faf6`, in conflict) as the fix. **Desk test 5 Oct (wasm32 SDK v2.1.0, offline, no broadcast):** same shape on `testnet-10` — `priorityFee` 0 and no `feeRate` → `Storage mass exceeds maximum`; `feeRate` 1 or 100 → 1 transaction; leftover 0.1 KAS with no `feeRate` → `Mass calculation error`. [#914](https://github.com/kaspanet/rusty-kaspa/issues/914) (RossKU, Covenant/KIP-16 code review, 5 findings at `10a4af3b`, 10 Mar) was closed as completed 4 Oct 21:32Z after atharaldsen [wrote](https://github.com/kaspanet/rusty-kaspa/issues/914#issuecomment-5984251477) that every finding is resolved on master. Desk spot-check at master `01b532e8`: `transaction_output_estimated_serialized_size` adds covenant bytes when present ([`mass/mod.rs`](https://github.com/kaspanet/rusty-kaspa/blob/01b532e8b553523216471682649693af92f0fd16/consensus/core/src/mass/mod.rs)); RPC `TryFrom<RpcTransactionOutput>` uses `with_covenant` ([`rpc/core/src/convert/tx.rs`](https://github.com/kaspanet/rusty-kaspa/blob/01b532e8b553523216471682649693af92f0fd16/rpc/core/src/convert/tx.rs)). Two of five claims checked; the rest are his reading. saefstroem: two pools above 50% of hashrate ([post](https://x.com/asaefstroem/status/2103861631738667208)), his chart, not recounted. Catalog.
